image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standalone single-storey small Bangkok Hospital clinic building, detailed front elevation with a glazed curtain-wall frontage and automatic doors under a shallow projecting entrance canopy, blue and white signage band carrying the Bangkok Hospital wordmark in Thai and English, white composite cladding panels across the upper front, plain warm cream painted side and rear walls in a single flat off-white tone clearly lighter than the background, with a service door and high windows, flat roof with a low parapet and roof-mounted air-conditioning condensers Materials: white composite cladding and blue printed sign face at the front, clear curtain-wall glazing, flat warm cream painted render on side and rear walls, galvanised roof plant.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless MID-DARK neutral grey (#606060), distinctly darker than every part of the building so the object reads as a clean cut-out against it. The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow. Apart from the building's own signage described above, there is no other text or lettering anywhere in the frame.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Real trademark: Bangkok Hospital / BDMS. The repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark; anyone shipping it needs their own trademark clearance.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT (v2 rebuild). Overall visual fidelity 0.85 -- not a pass self-score. 968/16000 triangles, 11/12 draw calls, 7/8 materials, 11/16 unique geometries. The plate's -X canopy wrap is the one feature knowingly left out (shared 8.00 m module).

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m (render bounds). Cream box capped at 4.15, white block to 4.60, canopy nose at z=3.50. Meshy proxy height map: cream parapet 0.88 H against the white top at 0.94 H, matched by 4.15/4.60 = 0.90.
featureReviews.notes: Band table residual is the DECLARED aspect, not the build: candidate w/h 1.718 vs 8/4.6 = 1.739; the proxy's d/w is 0.95 against the declared 0.875. The proxy's +0.12 H width bump at 45% height is the canopy wrapping the -X corner, which is NOT built: it cannot fit inside the shared 8.00 m module. Recorded as the one silhouette event the plate shows and the prop does not.

featureReviews.evidence: Two boards side by side on the +Z front, as the plate shows: white 'Bangkok Hospital' with a Thai subtitle on blue (x -0.65..3.85) and blue text on a white board (x -3.85..-0.85). One canvas split at u=0.5, one material, one draw call.
featureReviews.notes: v1 put the second board on the -X wall, misreading the plate: both signs are on the front. The blue stays lifted to #3B7BD8 from the measured #1C498B for the luma-only silhouette gate. The white board names its own plain-UV corner so its 0.06 m edges are white, not the canvas blue.

featureReviews.evidence: Top to bottom: panelled cladding with six joints (3.70..4.60), sign band (2.96..3.68), strip window (2.35..2.95, six bars), canopy slab (2.15..2.35), ground glazing with six mullions and a sliding-door bay. Two stacked four-pane windows on +X at 2.40..3.45 and 0.55..1.80, z 0.90..2.10, and the flush door behind them.
featureReviews.notes: The white block is a 0.75 m deep full-height volume, which is what gives the ~0.7 m white return at each front corner the plate shows. Panel joints are the framing aluminium (#b1b8bf) on #c4c8ce cladding -- subtle, as they are in the plate. The interior seen through the plate's glazing is not modelled: exterior shell.

featureReviews.evidence: A 0.20 m thick slab projecting 0.58 m off the block face to z=3.50, the full 8.00 m width, with a visible edge fascia at every turntable azimuth.
featureReviews.notes: Projection is what the declared depth leaves after a 6.34 m box; the plate's own is nearer 0.8 m. The -X wrap is not built (see overall-silhouette).
